subject: BYOK visibility runbook — product asks & sampling exception
messages:
From: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@clearwell-health.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: BYOK keystore visibility + sampling for short-term retention

Hi Soojin / Ben,

Thanks again for the call last week. We're trying to finalize our audit evidence checklist for the pilot and have a couple of follow ups that are blocking our internal sign-off:

- Can Redwood provide a short runbook describing how BYOK key operations are surfaced in audit logs (key_id, key rotation events, which tenant can see metadata)?
- We have a compliance constraint that requires holding session-level records for 30 days, but only for sessions flagged as "sensitive" (~4% of traffic). Is there an option to sample or mark sessions such that we only retain full traces for flagged sessions while keeping aggregated counters for others?

Attached is our evidence requirements summary for context. Can you confirm what we should expect in terms of log fields and a tentative timeframe for a runbook/copy of evidence?

Appreciate a short call if needed — we want to avoid a long procurement delay.

Thanks,
Alicia
Director, Compliance
Clearwell Health
(attachment: clearwell_evidence_requirements.pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@clearwell-health.com>, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, chris@secconsultant.io
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK keystore visibility + sampling for short-term retention

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Quick response and plan below; attaching a draft runbook and a small CSV mapping to illustrate which fields we can provide.

Short answers:
- BYOK visibility: we capture key operations (create/rotate/destroy) with key_id, actor, timestamp, and operation_type. These events are emitted to the tenant audit stream but we can include an additional per-tenant metadata tag if you need clearer scoping.
- Session sampling: we don't currently support on-the-fly per-session retention toggles in the hosted product, but we do support "sensitive session tagging" at the application layer which triggers retention to a longer-lived evidence bucket for that session. We can propose a rollout path to make tagging plumbed into the runtime in Q4.

Proposed triage (action items):
1) Product to confirm ETA for adding a retention-tag hook in the runtime (Ben + Jordan) — request: estimate by end of week.
2) Security to review the runbook for required fields and sign off on the export format (Kim).
3) If Product needs more time, Redwood can offer a temporary evidence-forwarding pattern where flagged sessions are forwarded to a Clearwell S3 bucket for 30 days (requires customer S3 and cross-account IAM).

Next steps: I'm free for a 30-min sync today at 3pm PT — propose that if you want to go over the runbook.

Attachments: draft_runbook_v0.1.pdf, sample_log_map.csv

—
Soojin Lee
Security PM, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
(attachment: sample_log_map.csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com, Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@clearwell-health.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK keystore visibility + sampling for short-term retention

Thanks — quick technical note on feasibility and constraints.

- Audit events: the runtime already emits keystore operations to the audit pipeline. We can add the tenant-scoped tag without perf impact. Fields available today: event_id, event_type, key_id (hashed), timestamp, actor_id, request_id, region, model_id. We can also add "key_rotation_reason" if you need it verbatim.
- Session tagging: the current hosted implementation stores KV cache and short-lived traces in hot storage; retaining full traces for ~4% of sessions would increase storage/dedup costs noticeably.

Workaround (short-term):
- Implement a lightweight header that the customer can set at ingestion (x-redwood-retain: sensitive) — the pipeline will fork the full trace to an evidence bucket (configurable S3). Minimal changes to runtime, high confidence, can be done as a patch in ~3 weeks.

I've uploaded a sample mapping that shows which fields we can deliver to Clearwell's S3 export. See sample_log_map.csv in the thread. If you can confirm required schema fields, I'll scope the export pipeline change and open a JIRA.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(attachment: sample_log_map.csv)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@clearwell-health.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK keystore visibility + sampling exception

Appreciate the clear options. Product take and next steps: 

1) We can accept the retention-tag hook as a Q4 product spike (non-blocking for pilot) — scope: runtime header + export pipeline fork + per-tenant config UI. Rough estimate: 2 sprints of eng + 1 week of QA. I'll create JIRA-7778 and link the runbook.
2) For the short-term procurement ask, approve the evidence-forwarding pattern (S3) as an interim solution — requires Clearwell to provision a cross-account bucket and minimal IAM. (Alicia — is that something you can spin up?)
3) Kim, please confirm if the fields in sample_log_map.csv meet Clearwell's audit evidence minimum. If anything else is required (e.g., full plaintext key IDs instead of hashed), we should capture the risk and whether an exception is needed.

I'll schedule a 30-min alignment tomorrow at 11am PT and include a short decision note for the execs. Soojin, please attach the runbook link (Drive) in the meeting invite.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
